comment: Sites exercising docs/GENERATION.md §6, one per canonical situation. Mined from data/overture-ch/preview.arpa (Montreux extract, z16) with `arpentry_verify <archive> --mine`. Each is the strongest instance the data holds, not a guess: re-mine after retiling a different extract. Use with `arpentry_verify <archive> --scenario S5`.

sites.source: mined: motorway deck standing 75 m above the drawn ground — the tallest viaduct in the extract, and worth confirming is real rather than phantom
mined: footway deck clearing the ground by only 2 m — S1's degenerate case, a deck that is nearly a chord
mined: 9 decks over at-grade road in one tile, all at level 1 — the densest crossing stack in the extract
mined: narrow_gauge bore under 599 m of hill — the deepest cover in the extract; a plausible Alpine rail tunnel, but the depth is worth confirming against the level ordinal it came from
mined: 6 bores under an at-grade road — the urban underpass case
mined: a deck and a bore in the same tile — bridge into tunnel, or close enough to inspect
mined: at-grade road at 28 % grade — the steepest carriageway still plausible as a real road, where the correct action is to do nothing

hand-sited 2026-08-21: three standard-gauge lines crossing Chemin de Vau over the road's cut at Burier, on mapped decks 10 m long while the road's band reaches 14 m along each of them. Before the deck annex the formation bands beside those decks still shared the road band's plan position: order.grade_stack 157 samples, 100 % over, worst 6.69 m (rail formation 396.7 m over the road at 390.0 m, nothing between them). After it the metric has no population here at all — the bands no longer overlap

hand-sited 2026-08-20: the Chauderon slot at Route de Chernex — a refused notch (deeper than the fill cap) crossed transversely by streets mapped at grade. Before the span-promotion fix: contact.kerb_lip 25.7 % over (worst 15.8 m) and order.deck_above_carriageway 25.6 % over (footbridge 15.2 m under at-grade asphalt). After promotion, approach absorption and the carried stubs: 21.4 % (worst 14.7 m) and 11.1 % (worst −10.8 m), with contact.kerb_unwalled 0 % throughout — what is left is a walled terrace whose walls are all drawn, not a dammed slot

hand-sited 2026-08-20: the Vernex-Dessus terrace — the MOB covered approach running parallel beneath the town streets, roof 6.5 m above the carved ground; clearance.bore_cover 71 % over in this tile before the parallel-overlap burial license

unsited.why: River bridge on flat ground. Needs the water layer decoded to find a deck over a river rather than over a ravine; the verifier reads only terrain and transportation today.

Dual carriageway on one structure. Needs parallel-structure identity, which the archive does not carry — two decks side by side are indistinguishable from one dual deck. Site by hand from the solved model (graph::parallel_structure_unions).
Annotation noise. Defined by its input, not its output: the site is a span that overlaps or leaves a sliver in the source, so it must come from the scene graph, not the archive.
Building on a steep slope. Needs the building layer decoded.
Dense old town with courtyards. Needs the building layer decoded.
Building beside a road cut. Needs the building layer decoded.
Lakefront. Needs the water layer decoded. Lake Geneva is in the extract, so this is the cheapest of the seven to add.

Level crossing. Needs the derived crossing set: a road and a rail surface coincident at grade is an equality the archive cannot distinguish from two unrelated features that happen to touch. Sites from the solved model once crossings are derived per stratum.
Street-running tram. Needs modality in the archive: the transportation layer carries class and level, and a tram class is not yet distinguished from the street it lies on.
Rack railway on a 45 % flank. Needs rail profiles and the per-class grade shape. The Rochers-de-Naye line is in the extract, so this sites itself as soon as R is solved.
Aqueduct on a viaduct. Needs water carried as a structure attribute (the back-edge rule); nothing in the model expresses it yet.
